decisions.reason: The definition constructs the distributional curl and graph norm on every open subset of R^3. A polyhedron is a special case, so the narrower title makes no unsupported mathematical assertion; the L2 uniqueness and test-continuity arguments are valid with the declared Countable Choice convention.

The graph-closure Definition is sound for arbitrary open sets, but its Remark attributes an unqualified boundary trace assertion to a lemma restricted to bounded Lipschitz polyhedra with a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh. Qualified only that Remark to the cited domain and trace-quotient convention; the Definition and all mathematical closure interfaces are unchanged.

The classical surface formula needs boundary values, whereas unspecified smoothness can mean only interior smoothness. This is a nonfatal regularity-convention omission: the quotient functional, its sqrt(2) bound and the zero-trace closure conclusion are proved correctly. Specified C1 fields on a neighborhood of the closure in the Statement and step 1.2, so u cross v satisfies the exact closed-cell Gauss–Green hypothesis; mirrored that step in the contract.

The correction lemma Statement explicitly adopts the hypotheses and notation of lem-na-whitney-averaged-pullback-moment-bounds. That supplier Statement defines the relative spaces by vanishing boundary moments and explicitly identifies them with E_h^k intersect H_0 Lambda^k; its proof 2.2 proves both inclusions using zero extension, outward smoothing and boundary surface distributions. The correction preserves that target by an inverse on the same finite-dimensional subcomplex. Thus F1 supplies the claimed homogeneous target through its inherited notation; no dependency or proof gap exists.
